newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-COUPLES SINKS BIRDIE PUTT TO CLINCH PRESIDENTS CUP FOR U.S.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-COUPLES SINKS BIRDIE PUTT TO CLINCH PRESIDENTS CUP FOR U.S.

text.p: Fred Couples sank a long birdie putt on the 17th hole to close out Vijay Singh and clinch the United States' second straight Presidents Cup title on Sunday at the Robert Trent Jones Golf Club.

Greg Norman defeated Corey Pavin 3 and 1 to lift the International team into a tie with the United States at 15 1/2 points each, leaving the verdict up to the last singles of the day between Couples and Singh.
Couples clinched the see-saw matches for the United States with a 2 and 1 win to avoid a playoff.
The United States, who had led the International team by one point heading into the final day, started off by winning three of the first five matches completed.
American Steve Stricker scored a convincing victory over Robert Allenby 6 and 5, David Duval beat Peter Senior 3 and 2, and Mark O'Meara edged Nick Price 1 up.
The International Team hung in, with wins posted by David Frost and Craig Parry. Frost dominated Kenny Perry 7 and 6, and Parry defeated Mark Brooks 5 and 4.

Davis Love III gave the United States a two-point lead by defeating Jumbo Ozaki 5 and 4. But the International team rallied to take the lead when Steve Elkington, Ernie Els and Frank Nobilo defeated their American rivals.
Elkington defeated Justin Leonard 1 up, Els downed Phil Mickelson 3 and 2, and Nobilo beat British Open champion Tom Lehman 3 and 2.
Scott Hoch gave the lead back to the United States by beating Mark McNulty 1 up, before Norman evened the competition with his victory over Pavin.
The International team had cut the lead to one point Saturday after taking three of five matches in the four-balls competition and four of five in the alternate-shot foursomes Saturday.
The United States captured the inaugural Presidents Cup two years ago and won by a lopsided 20-12 margin.
